summary: Removes node a2 from a category-tagged doubly-linked list and decrements the corresponding category counter. The node's low three bits (*a2 & 7) select which of three counter/head pairs on `this` to update (cases 1, 2, 4); otherwise the node itself is treated as its own counter/head slot. After unlink, if the selected head equals the removed node the head advances to node->next.

operations.description: Switch on *a2 & 7 selecting the category-specific counter/head pair: case 1 uses this+71/this+72, case 2 uses this+75/this+76, case 4 uses this+73/this+74 (byte offsets 0x124 counter and 0x128 head), default uses the node itself for both.
Save the node's backward link: v4 = a2[26] (prev pointer, byte offset 104).
If v4 (prev) is non-null, set prev's forward link: *(v4 + 108) = a2[27] (next).
Save the node's forward link: v5 = a2[27] (next pointer, byte offset 108).
If v5 (next) is non-null, set next's backward link: *(v5 + 104) = a2[26] (prev).
If the selected head (*v3) equals the removed node, advance the head to the node's next: *v3 = a2[27].
Decrement the selected category counter: --*result (this 0x124 for case 4).
Return the counter pointer that was decremented.

clean_pseudocode: case 1: counter = this + 71; head = this + 72; break;
case 2: counter = this + 75; head = this + 76; break;
case 4: counter = this + 73; head = this + 74; break;
default: counter = node; head = node; break;
unresolved: The meaning of the 3-bit category tag (1/2/4) in *a2 is not established here.
The callers sub_5454A0 and LinkedListWalkWithDispatch determine which node type and list instances are affected.
